newsitem.title: UK: Former Barings boss Baker wins appeal against SFA.
newsitem.headline: Former Barings boss Baker wins appeal against SFA.

text.p: Former Barings executive Ron Baker on Wednesday succeeded in an appeal against a Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) ruling that he had been guilty of misconduct, the British financial watchdog said.

"By winning his appeal today, Mr Baker has successfully rebutted all the charges brought by the SFA against him following the failure of Barings," SFA chairman Nick Durlacher said in a statement. The decision brings the SFA's actions relating to the collapse of merchant bank Barings in 1995 to a close.

Durlacher said he was satisfied that the SFA's disciplinary process had been seen to work. Baker, who represented himself at the appeal, was challenging a disciplinary tribunal which found he had been guilty of an act of misconduct.

The SFA brought disciplinary proceedings against nine former Barings directors in March 1996. But it did not proceed against Peter Baring and Andrew Tuckey, chairman and deputy chairman of the Barings group at the time of its spectacular collapse.

Barings went bust in February 1995 under the weight of some 800 million pounds ($1.3 billion) of losses racked up in unauthorised derivatives trades by Singapore-based trader Nick Leeson, who is now languishing in a Singapore jail.
Barings was rescued by Dutch financial services group Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV and now operates as ING Barings.
